sentence: This project studies how genetic variation controls heat tolerance and drug resistance in fungal pathogens that live in the environment.
This project studies how astrocytes remodel the synapses and neurons that drive cocaine seeking.
This project tests a treatment for a jaw disease in rice rats by delivering an engineered fusion protein to the lesion site.
This project uses genetic methods in Mycobacterium tuberculosis to find combinations of drug targets that could shorten tuberculosis treatment.
This project studies how airway cells are renewed after lung transplantation and how the immune system destroys airway stem cells.
This project studies how children come to use digital media and how those patterns predict mental health and heart health over time.
This project uses Micro-OrganoSpheres to study how host and microbe interact, how nearby cells affect each other, and how stem cells choose their fate.
This project builds a tool that uses machine learning to bring together and examine a database on the safety and toxicity of excipients for children.
This project maps how tau pathology disrupts the proteome in Alzheimer's disease, at the level of cell types and molecules.
This project uses a mouse model of triple negative breast cancer to find genetic modifiers of tumor aggression and response to therapy.
This project studies a type of immune cell in the gut that makes a protein called granzyme A and may harm the gut lining.
This project studies how glia cells and signaling pathways drive the growth of new neurons in the adult Drosophila brain.
This project studies the genetic landscape and evolution of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
This project combines technologies into a double-encapsulation system for delivering nerve growth factor and tests it in a mouse spinal cord injury model.
This project uses single-cell methods to study T cell traits and gene signatures linked to relapse after stem-cell transplantation in patients with myelodysplastic syndromes.
This project uses imaging of the heart to understand changes in myocardial thickness and tissue that can lead to abnormal heart rhythms.
This project studies the genetic and epigenetic factors behind Ph-like acute lymphoblastic leukemia in Hispanic and Latino populations.
This project studies how modular polyketide synthases in bacteria work, using structure tools on an antibiotic-producing assembly line.
This project builds a blood-brain barrier assembloid with Alzheimer's-associated risk variants to find how they cause the barrier to break down.
This project tests whether gut microbes changed by obesity raise cancer risk by disrupting protective immunity.
